title: Biomarker endpoint assessment for clinical outcomes in acute kidney injury
summary: MAKE90, a combined measure of serious renal events within 90 days, is often used but has weaknesses: The time period is often too short for reliable long-term results, very different events (death, dialysis dependence, persistent loss of function) are mixed together, and percentage changes in creatinine can lead to misclassifications in patients who are already ill or unstable. Therefore, a new, risk-based composite endpoint with clear clinical criteria is needed. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common after major surgery and is closely linked to chronic kidney disease (CKD); available biomarkers enable early risk detection. The new endpoint should therefore combine clinically detectable AKI complications with a biomarker-based classification. Secondary objectives include the frequency of CKD, the influence of perioperative factors on CKD, and outcomes such as length of stay and mortality, as well as the need for renal replacement therapy and its effects.

interventions.name: Patients who have undergone major surgery are included in the study postoperatively if certain risk factors are present, and biological samples (blood and urine) are taken. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Major surgery (cardiac surgery, abdominal surgery, and vascular surgery) with a duration of > 2h
- Planned admission to the Intensive Care Unit, Intermediate Care or PACU after surgery
- One of the following Risk factors:
a.	Age >70 years
b.	Use of catecholamines
c.	CKD
d.	Mechanical ventilated
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Pre-existing AKI 
- Kidney transplantation within the last 12 Months
- End stage renal disease with dialysis dependency
- COPD requiring permanent oxygen therapy
- Alzheimer disease or dementia of any kind
- High doses of corticosteroids (cutoff: Prednisolone (7,5 mg) or hydrocortisone (>3 mg form men, > 20 mg for women) )
- Any form of dependency to the investigators
